Cross Canada meetings by monthMeetings held, May – Oct 2026

Highlights since the tours

  • West tour completed — Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta and British Columbia (May 19 – Jun 13), then Newfoundland & Labrador and Nova Scotia by video.
  • Time to Attach: federal announcement tentatively set for Dec 10 (confidential until confirmed); ESDC had been hopeful for year-end implementation.
  • Labour ministries: Saskatchewan, Alberta and Nova Scotia briefed; BC to be rescheduled after the snap election; PEI Nov 9.
  • AFCCA: Alberta Family Ministry very interested; Newfoundland & Labrador asked the MCCSS Child Welfare Secretariat to invite Interwoven to present to all provincial Deputy Ministers and ADMs.
  • Ontario: every organization met said yes to working together, as reported in the Ontario dashboard.

Ontario Connections Trip · Northern Ontario · May – Sept 2025Ontario trip review

A small team drove across Northern Ontario to share Interwoven's programs, build partnerships and learn what families and workers need. Every organization visited said yes to working together.

Regions visitedParry Sound (May 11) is counted in North Bay

  • North Bay – May 7–8
  • Sudbury – May 11
  • Sault Ste. Marie – May 12
  • Timmins – May 13 and Sept 17 (Inspire)
  • Thunder Bay – May 14–15
  • Kenora – Aug 12 (Firefly)

Who we met17 meetings & events by type

The big picture

  • New partnerships: every organization visited said yes to working together.
  • Sharing programs: tools and training for workers supporting children with trauma and families in adoption or kinship care.
  • Indigenous communities: 3 Indigenous-led organizations keen to bring culturally relevant resources to their communities.
  • French language: need identified for French resources and bilingual support.
  • Fall events: several organizations want Interwoven at September Kinship Awareness Week events.

The team

  • Erin Perron – Team Lead; led in-person meetings and relationship building
  • Julie Despaties – Executive Director; strategic leadership and regional representation
One extra virtual meeting was held June 16 with Métis Nation of Ontario because of scheduling conflicts during the tour.

Key interests expressed

  • AFCCA training (Polyvagal & NVR) – 6+ organizations

  • AFCCA Community of Practice – 2
  • French resources – NEOFACS

  • Virtual grandmother / kinship groups – NAN Legal, TBIFC, Métis Nation

New trends identified

  • Foster parents & children: why aren't they getting AFCCA support?
  • Time to Attach: parents not receiving leave (Sudbury, Algoma CAS)
  • Indigenous grandmothers often navigate kinship care alone
  • Urgent response: Inspire reports about 90% of its URS cases involve aggression
  • Referral gap: CAS want Interwoven referrals at placement

Impact on families & caregivers

  • Indigenous grandmothers caring alone identified as a critical unserved group; virtual support groups being planned.
  • Foster and kinship families need expanded AFCCA support, now championed provincially by One Kids Place.
  • French-speaking families to benefit from bilingual programming being developed with NEOFACS.
  • A culturally grounded colouring book is being co-developed with Anishinabek Nation.

Impact on systems & organizations

  • Several CAS are seeking to change referral processes to include Interwoven at placement.
  • One Kids Place's manager joined the PNCA working group to advance the AFCCA proposal provincially.
  • Co-delivery of childcare at kinship events is being explored with Thrive Child Development Centre.
  • AFCCA resource translation into Indigenous languages is underway with Anishinabek Nation.

Potential future impact

  • If all four CAS Awareness Week events proceed, 200+ additional kinship caregivers could be reached during Kinship Awareness Week.
  • Provincial advocacy through PNCA could expand AFCCA support beyond public adoption.
  • French-language programming could serve hundreds of francophone families; Indigenous translation could open the tools to First Nations communities for the first time.
  • Firefly Kenora and Dryden extend the network into Northwestern Ontario.

Source: Interwoven Connections Ontario Trip Review dashboard. Thunder Bay is shown as 16 (including a 3-person community dinner) so regions add to the 109 total; the dashboard chart showed 13, which would sum to 106. The dashboard headline cards state 14 organizations and 23 meetings & events; the dashboard meeting table supports 15 organizations and 17 meetings & events held, which are the figures used here. Kilometres, driving hours and staff count are carried from the dashboard as reported.

The big picture

  • Coast-to-coast reach: 4 provinces on tour, then Newfoundland & Labrador and Nova Scotia by video; PEI booked Nov 9.
  • Time to Attach is moving: ESDC hopeful for end-of-year implementation; Saskatchewan, Alberta and Nova Scotia labour ministries briefed.
  • Caregivers are speaking up: Evermore Centre held its first kinship group and is launching a support group.
  • Indigenous-led partners engaged: NCTR (three meetings), Ma Mawi Wi Chi Itata and Surrounded by Cedar.
  • Fall invitations: Victoria Foundation, and a possible presentation to all provincial Deputy Ministers and ADMs via MCCSS.

Impact on families & caregivers

  • Evermore Centre held its first kinship caregiver group; caregivers described the silence and shame they carry.
  • Fairness for Grandparents and the Calgary caregiver group asked for more AFCCA content.
  • KFFNM wants to share AFCCA resources with members; more work is needed on the needs of kinship and customary caregivers welcoming older youth.
  • Indigenous communities are exploring adapted AFCCA and FASD&ME resources via Manitoba Families and Ma Mawi.

Impact on systems & governments

  • ESDC hopeful for end-of-year Time to Attach implementation.
  • Saskatchewan, Alberta and Nova Scotia labour ministries briefed; BC to be rescheduled after the snap election; PEI Nov 9.
  • Alberta Family Ministry very interested in AFCCA; Calgary and Edmonton meetings held.
  • UNBC and University of Victoria lining up around the next research phase (Oct 28).

Participants by region

  • Time to Attach announcement and a possible federal rollout around year-end.
  • Provincial rollout: BC and Saskatchewan need legislation; Nova Scotia, Alberta and PEI conversations under way or booked.
  • National audience for AFCCA via a presentation to all provincial Deputy Ministers and ADMs.
  • An Alberta-led AFCCA pilot.
  • Funding and research: Belonging Network (CoE), Victoria Foundation, UNBC / UVic.
  • Culturally grounded resources with Indigenous-led partners in Manitoba.

Time to Attach · National Campaign, Phase TwoEquity for kinship & customary caregivers

The goal: ALL permanency parents benefit from the new EI benefits when implemented. Momentum is real — a federal announcement is tentatively set for December 10.

🔒 CONFIDENTIAL — board and invited partners only. Do not share this section outside the Interwoven Board and invited partners until the date is confirmed (expected mid-November).

🎉 A decade in the making: federal Time to Attach legislative change

Allies and researchBuilding alliances across the country

  • UNBC & University of Victoria — research phase on kinship and customary care (Oct 28).
  • NCTR (Winnipeg) — exploring introductions to key organizations; three meetings to date.
  • Documentary on kinship grandparents — may connect for advocacy insights at tour screenings.
  • Parent Support BC and Fairness for Grandparents — caregiver voices in BC.
  • Nova Scotia asked how to engage C-92 Governing Bodies for customary caregivers.

Action items — Time to Attach

  • Reconnect with the BC Minister of Children & Family Development.
  • Reschedule the BC Labour Ministry meeting after the election.
  • Follow up with Alberta Labour on the new leave and on including kinship and customary caregivers.
  • Follow up with Saskatchewan Labour (ADM) on readiness to legislate.
  • Prepare for PEI (Nov 9); track ESDC timing and the federal announcement.
